overview: Cardiomegaly refers to an enlarged heart silhouette observed on diagnostic thoracic imaging. Rather than a distinct disease entity itself, it is a clinical radiographic sign of underlying myocardial hypertrophy, ventricular dilation, or pericardial fluid accumulation.
radiographic_findings: Cardiothoracic Ratio (CTR) exceeding 0.50 on a standard upright PA projection (cardiac width divided by maximum internal thoracic diameter)
Left heart border lateral extension and downward rounding indicating left ventricular enlargement
Double density of the right cardiac margin indicating left atrial enlargement
Cephalization of pulmonary vessels or Kerley B lines if accompanied by pulmonary venous hypertension
common_symptoms: Shortness of breath on exertion (dyspnea) or while lying flat (orthopnea)
Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea (waking up gasping for air)
Peripheral edema (swelling in the lower legs, ankles, or feet)
Fatigue, reduced exercise tolerance, and rapid exhaustion
Heart palpitations, irregular pulse, or chest heaviness
causes_and_risk_factors: Long-standing systemic arterial hypertension (high blood pressure)
Coronary artery disease and prior myocardial infarction
Valvular heart disease (aortic stenosis, mitral regurgitation)
Pericardial effusion (fluid within the pericardial sac)
Congenital heart defects and chronic severe anemia
diagnostic_information: Transthoracic Echocardiography (TTE) - primary gold standard to assess ejection fraction and chamber dimensions
12-Lead Electrocardiogram (ECG) to assess rhythm and voltage criteria for ventricular hypertrophy
Biomarkers: Serum B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) or NT-proBNP
Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging (CMR) for myocardial tissue characterization
treatment_approaches: Aggressive blood pressure control with ACE inhibitors, ARBs, or ARNIs
Beta-blockers (e.g., carvedilol, metoprolol succinate) to reduce myocardial workload
Diuretics (e.g., furosemide) for volume overload and edema management
SGLT2 inhibitors and aldosterone receptor antagonists for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
Dietary sodium restriction and monitored fluid intake
when_to_seek_care: Acute, crushing substernal chest discomfort or pain radiating to jaw or left arm
Severe acute shortness of breath occurring at rest
Sudden significant weight gain (2-3 lbs in 24 hours) with rapidly worsening edema
